title: Turmeric golden decoction
subtitle: A daily anti-inflammatory decoction of Curcuma longa root for chronic low-grade inflammation
excerpt: Turmeric decoction is dried or fresh Curcuma longa root simmered in water with black pepper and a small amount of fat, strained and drunk warm as a daily anti-inflammatory preparation. Black pepper is added because piperine increases curcumin absorption by up to 2000%. Traditionally taken for chronic musculoskeletal inflammation, joint stiffness, and digestive inflammatory conditions. One cup per day. Not for use at high doses in pregnancy.
sourceNotes: WHO Monographs on Selected Medicinal Plants Volume 1 (1999), Rhizoma Curcumae Longae, open access. Shoba G et al., Influence of piperine on the pharmacokinetics of curcumin in animals and human volunteers, Planta Medica (1998), piperine bioavailability data. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Curcuma longa L., rhizoma (2018, EMA/HMPC/671516/2017).

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 cup of herbal brew (1 day's dose)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried turmeric stores 12 months in a sealed jar. Decoct fresh each day.

glossaryTerms.definition: The primary curcuminoid compound in Curcuma longa root, responsible for its yellow colour and most of its studied anti-inflammatory effects. Curcumin has poor bioavailability when taken alone, piperine from black pepper and fat in the preparation significantly increase absorption.

The active alkaloid in black pepper (Piper nigrum) that inhibits the liver enzyme responsible for rapidly breaking down curcumin, dramatically increasing the amount that reaches the bloodstream. Adding black pepper to turmeric preparations is not incidental, it is essential for efficacy.

content.text: Turmeric golden brew is dried root simmered in water with black pepper and a little fat. It is strained and drunk warm. Black pepper is key:
, so without it most of the active compound passes through unused. Taken daily for joint stiffness and long-term low-grade inflammation. Golden, warming, faintly bitter.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

items.prepNote: freshly ground black pepper, do not skip
coconut oil or ghee, fat is needed for curcumin absorption

content.text: Place 1 teaspoon of turmeric powder, a pinch of black pepper, and 1 teaspoon of coconut oil in a small saucepan. Add 250 ml of water.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, whisking to combine the fat into the liquid. Simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.
Strain through a fine strainer into a mug. Sweeten with a little honey if preferred. Drink warm.
One cup daily, taken consistently for a minimum of 8 weeks to assess the effect on chronic inflammation. Turmeric acts slowly and cumulatively, do not expect acute results.
Dried turmeric powder stores 12 months in a sealed jar. Decoct each cup fresh.
When not to use this remedy

Avoid high-dose use in pregnancy and with anticoagulant medication without professional advice. See a doctor for joint swelling or pain that is new, worsening, or limiting movement. These may need investigation before herbal support.
